# Run quarantined Linux tests in the Azure Linux test container

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

Align quarantined Linux tests with the regular Azure Linux test environment.

## Description

The quarantined Linux job already inherits an Azure Linux 3 build agent after #70558, but still runs directly on that agent and is labeled "Ubuntu x64".

- Reuse the regular Linux test job's `azurelinux-4.0-net12.0-build-aot-test-nginx-amd64` image.
- Run the quarantined Linux job inside that container.
- Rename its display name to `Tests: Azure Linux x64`.

The container provides the host-native NativeAOT test toolchain, Nginx, and other test prerequisites introduced in #70637. It is not a shipping-artifact cross-build image. The underlying Azure Linux 3 agent selection is unchanged.

Preserve the build and test commands, `RunQuarantinedTests=true`, `SkipHelixReadyTests=true`, `continueOnError: true`, result publication, artifacts, timeout, triggers, and all other jobs. No host configuration changes are introduced.

### Validation

- `python3 -` with PyYAML structural assertions — passed. Both pipeline files parse, the image resource exactly matches `ci-public.yml`, and removing only the new resource/container selection and reverting the display name reproduces the original quarantine pipeline structure.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Container prerequisite smoke check — passed:

  ```bash
  docker run --rm mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs:azurelinux-4.0-net12.0-build-aot-test-nginx-amd64 bash -lc 'set -e; cat /etc/os-release; command -v bash git clang gcc ld nginx node npm java; clang --version | head -1; nginx -v; nginx -t; node --version; npm --version; java -version; test -n "$JAVA_HOME"; test -e /usr/lib64/libatomic.so.1'
  ```

  Confirmed Azure Linux 4, clang 21.1.8, Nginx 1.30.6 with valid configuration, Node/npm, JDK 25, and libatomic. The locally tested image digest is `sha256:b9f646b6b8fe4665f791ee51d0e35a6145dd1923083e4387161de9affa92ab07`.

### Containerized CI execution

The changed Linux job completed in [build 1686952](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1686952&view=logs&jobId=716f19c4-d2e3-58b0-1706-7999a9b178f6), testing PR source commit `ef0161f859239450c1600a10ca748e5e131f36e9`.

- Container initialization — passed; CI pulled the same image digest tested locally.
- `./eng/build.sh --ci --nobl --all --no-build-java --pack` — passed, exit 0.
- `./eng/build.sh --ci --nobl --all --no-build --no-build-java --test -p:RunQuarantinedTests=true -p:SkipHelixReadyTests=true` — executed and exited 1 for the pre-existing quarantined `LinkedApplicationWorks` failure described below.
- `Publish Quarantined Test Results` and result-artifact publication — passed.

I inspected the published xUnit XML, rather than treating the job's green GitHub check as proof of test success:

| Published results | Before: build 1686691 | Container: build 1686952 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passed | 9 | 10 |
| Failed | 2 | 1 |
| Skipped | 11 | 11 |

Both runs selected the same 22 test cases, including the same guaranteed-quarantine sentinel cases and platform skips. The Nginx `ServerComparison.FunctionalTests.HelloWorldTests.HelloWorld` case now **passes**; before this change it failed because `nginx` was not installed on the bare build agent.

`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.FunctionalTests.LinkedApplicationTests.LinkedApplicationWorks` still fails before reaching its HTTP response/body assertion. In **both** runs its published `BasicLinkedApp` crashes with the same `FileNotFoundException` for the managed assembly `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Transport.Quic, Version=12.0.0.0`. This is an existing quarantined application-publishing failure, not addressed by the container change.

The Linux job is reported as `succeededWithIssues` because quarantined test failures deliberately retain `continueOnError: true`. This PR does not claim all quarantined tests pass. Other CI checks are still in progress.

Disable HTTP/1.x CONNECT connection reuse regardless of response status.

## Description

Extends https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67929 to disable keep-alive for HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 CONNECT responses regardless of the final status, including 2xx. This goes beyond RFC 9931 Section 8, which requires closure only for rejected HTTP/1.1 CONNECT requests. HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and ordinary non-CONNECT connection reuse are unchanged.

Fixes: N/A (no linked issue provided).

Switch the Playwright benchmark runtime image to Ubuntu 26.04 Resolute.

## Description

Two-line infrastructure change, on a standalone branch from `main`:

- Change the WASM performance benchmark's final-stage image from `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/dotnet:v1.62.0-noble-amd64` to `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/dotnet:v1.62.0-resolute-amd64`.
- Change the Selenium/Playwright dependency refresh script to select `-resolute-amd64` rather than `-noble-amd64`, so future refreshes retain the new distribution.

Keep Microsoft.Playwright at **1.62.0**, matching the existing package version, and retain amd64. No SDK/build-stage, package-version, agent-pool, browser-test framework, or shipping-product changes.

The official image contains Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon). Playwright documents the Resolute variant at https://playwright.dev/docs/docker.

Related to the merged #70558. Current `main` has been merged into this branch; the updater conflict was resolved by retaining Resolute.

### Validation

- MCR manifest lookup for `playwright/dotnet:v1.62.0-resolute-amd64` — HTTP 200.
- `docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/dotnet:v1.62.0-resolute-amd64` — passed. Digest: `sha256:92ed8dacdc5b13332964633f437c2cef4c44bf41440155dac442047b79b5741e`.
- `cat /etc/os-release` in the image — confirmed Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, `VERSION_CODENAME=resolute`.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File /updater-check.ps1` in the image — passed. The temporary check parses the complete refresh script, evaluates its actual image-tag assignment using Microsoft.Playwright 1.62.0, and invokes its actual `Update-Dockerfile` function on a temporary Dockerfile. It selects `v1.62.0-resolute-amd64`. It does not execute the script's dependency updates, commits, pushes, or PR creation.
- Parsed `eng/Versions.props` and checked that the final-stage image matches the unchanged Microsoft.Playwright package version — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- After merging `main`, `git diff origin/main --check` — passed. Rechecked the merged updater with `pwsh -NoProfile -Command -` in the Resolute image: full-script syntax parsing passed, and the actual image-tag assignment and runtime Dockerfile both match the package version, `v1.62.0-resolute-amd64`.

A temporary .NET console probe referencing Microsoft.Playwright **1.62.0**, using the activated repository SDK/runtime, ran inside the Resolute image:

```bash
dotnet bin/Release/net12.0/Probe.dll
```

Passed with exit 0, including three additional consecutive direct-launch checks: launched headless Chromium **151.0.7922.34** using the same `Chromium.LaunchAsync` and `en-US` page locale as the benchmark driver, navigated to a page, clicked a button through Playwright, and verified the resulting DOM and page title.

The first invocation through `dotnet run --project Probe.csproj --configuration Release` completed the browser assertions but then exited 139 with a process-reaping error (`Error while reaping child. errno = 10`). Running the built probe directly, without the extra SDK launcher process, completed cleanly and more closely matches the deployed benchmark driver's process shape. The initial launcher's shutdown failure was not independently root-caused.

This is an image/browser compatibility smoke check, not a full WASM performance benchmark or full multistage image build. No performance measurements or performance-equivalence claims are made.

# Clarify browser-observed rendering test boundaries

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [ ] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Clarify which rendering contracts require real-browser regression coverage.

## Description

Follow-up to #70411. Qualify "rendering or rehydration" as browser-observed behavior, such as DOM output or the prerender-to-interactive handoff in a real page. Explicitly retain managed RenderTree diffs and component or service state at the faithful lower boundary when fully owned and observable there, for example in a .NET unit test using `TestRenderer`.

Apply the same meaning in `src/Components/AGENTS.md` and `validate-blazor-feature`. No other test rule, skill description, eval stimulus, or rubric changes.

The QuickGrid discussion in [#67314](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67314#discussion_r4596001345) concerns a visible CSS indicator and a test that never renders its options button. This clarification does not establish that the real-browser coverage request in that comment was incorrect.

### Validation

- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .\eng\skill-evals\run.ps1 -Action Validate` - passed.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .\eng\skill-evals\run.ps1 -Action Test` - passed.
- Paid `skills-vs-baseline` comparison: nine selected stimuli, five trials per arm, two workers; all 90 planned trials completed with valid scores and no reported grader errors. No paid retries or rubric changes.

The paid run used the existing staging entry point and runner:

```powershell
& .\eng\skill-evals\stage_run.ps1 -TrustedRoot $repoRoot -CandidateRoot $repoRoot -EvalName 'validate-blazor-feature' -Destination $execRoot
foreach ($shard in @(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 14))
{
    $output = Join-Path $outBase ('shard-{0:d2}' -f $shard)
    & pwsh -NoProfile -File (Join-Path $execRoot 'eng\skill-evals\run.ps1') Run -Eval (Join-Path $execRoot 'eng\skill-evals\validate-blazor-feature\eval.vally.yaml') -OutputDirectory $output --shard "$shard/15" --shard-strategy by-stimulus --run-id $runId --workers 2
}
```

Seven stimuli overlap the #70411 run at `f62b811a1e`; the two additional cases exercise nondeterministic boundary selection and focus/selection after rerender. Each result below is **trials scoring at least 0.60 / 5; mean score**. Activation counts refer to native skill invocation in the skilled arm, not merely skill availability.

| Stimulus | Prior baseline | Prior skilled | Current baseline | Current skilled | Skill activations, prior -> current |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-pure-typescript-helper-test` | 2/5; 0.58 | 4/5; 0.70 | 0/5; 0.50 | 3/5; 0.60 | 1/5 -> 0/5 |
| `choose-selenium-for-real-browser-geometry` | 0/5; 0.28 | 5/5; 0.80 | 1/5; 0.36 | 5/5; 0.84 | 5/5 -> 5/5 |
| `deterministic-browser-probe-to-selenium` | 0/5; 0.36 | 5/5; 0.84 | 0/5; 0.32 | 5/5; 0.84 | 5/5 -> 5/5 |
| `keep-dom-sync-at-faithful-lower-boundary` | 3/5; 0.52 | 5/5; 0.92 | 2/5; 0.44 | 5/5; 1.00 | 5/5 -> 5/5 |
| `keep-endpoint-persistence-at-managed-boundary` | 2/5; 0.48 | 4/5; 0.64 | 3/5; 0.52 | 4/5; 0.56 | 1/5 -> 0/5 |
| `reject-fast-jest-only-observer-proof` | 0/5; 0.18 | 5/5; 0.92 | 0/5; 0.18 | 4/5; 0.80 | 5/5 -> 4/5 |
| `split-manager-contract-from-browser-reachability` | 4/5; 0.66 | 5/5; 0.92 | 4/5; 0.72 | 5/5; 0.90 | 5/5 -> 5/5 |
| `investigate-nondeterministic-browser-reproduction` | Not run | Not run | 5/5; 0.70 | 5/5; 0.96 | Not run -> 5/5 |
| `keep-selenium-with-minimal-javascript-step` | Not run | Not run | 5/5; 0.84 | 5/5; 1.00 | Not run -> 5/5 |

These are not uniformly green results. On the seven shared stimuli, skilled passes fell from 33/35 to 31/35 and the mean fell from 0.8200 to 0.7914. The managed-persistence slice falls below the configured 0.60 score threshold. The nine-stimulus skilled mean is 0.8333; that aggregate does not erase the individual misses.

The pass-count drops are in pure-helper and observer-proof trials that did not invoke the skill. The observer miss genuinely recommends insufficient Jest-only coverage; the pure-helper misses select the correct lower boundary but omit the required decision record. The managed-persistence miss omits the renderer producer and complete boundary record. All 34 current trials that invoked the skill scored at least 0.60, versus 11 that did not invoke it. There is also a smaller mean-score decline on the fully activated manager case (0.92 to 0.90), without a pass-count decline.

Actual subject and judge identities were checked from token-usage records and match the earlier run in both arms. Requested subject metadata differs from actual usage in both runs. These are small workflow-level samples, not evidence that the wording caused either improvements or regressions, and the managed-boundary cases' low activation limits what they establish about the edited skill body.

Independent wording and scope review found no issues before pushing.

# Add scoped Components code-review checks

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable. (Documentation-only; no runtime behavior changes.)
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Put compact Components review facts directly in path-scoped instructions.

## Description

Keep the existing links and path scopes, and add four focused review checks to the two Components instruction files:

- Case-insensitive `[Parameter]` name collisions across declared and inherited parameters, including the compatibility risk when adding a base-class parameter.
- The permanent-test boundary clarified in #70411: managed RenderTree/component/service contracts stay at a faithful .NET unit-test boundary; deterministic module contracts can use `Web.JS` `.test.ts`; browser-owned behavior uses the owning browser suite. Preserve the generated-template Playwright and existing Platform suite boundaries, and reject tests that never exercise or observe the intended contract. "Browser-observed rendering or rehydration" does not mean managed RenderTree output alone.
- Root-component operation ordering must not prevent a later removal from releasing an initialization task awaited for first-render quiescence.
- Synchronous circuit termination from an `UnhandledException` subscriber can disconnect the client before a later `JS.Error` notification.

The circuit checks are scoped to Server and Endpoints. Existing logging guidance is unchanged. This PR does not change `AGENTS.md`, skills, product code, public APIs, or test-suite policy.

Source verification used `main` at `f2484a6bf688bd1acb1af13802255c2c23a071dd`: `ComponentProperties`/`MemberAssignment`, the existing parameter-collision tests, `CircuitHost`, `CircuitRegistry`, the merged permanent-regression policy, and the existing Platform test suite. The ordering hazards are illustrated by the frozen #68633 proposal at `39b01416d015e6dda10381a4cb4a1487ac9bee80`; the instructions do not claim that current `main` already serializes batches that way.

Validation:

- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `npx --offline --yes --registry=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/ --package markdownlint-cli@0.45.0 markdownlint --disable MD041 -- .github\instructions\components.instructions.md .github\instructions\components.server.instructions.md` - passed. MD041 is excluded because these existing instruction fragments do not start with an H1; their original frontmatter and opening text are unchanged.
- Content checks passed: only the two intended files changed; existing content, links, and `applyTo` values are preserved; both files are ASCII and under 4 KB.
- An independent source review completed with no remaining findings after precision corrections.
- Runtime/browser tests were not run because no executable behavior changed.

### Paired CCR canary

Ran one old/new pair for each frozen historical change on `PureWeen/aspnetcore` (10 completed reviews). Both arms receive the same current instructions, skills, and normative Components policy over the historical product source; only these two instruction files differ between arms. Every fixture preserves its historical product diff exactly. Actions logs confirm the expected path-matched instructions were loaded in all 10 runs. Treatment wording matches this PR after line-ending normalization.

| Historical change | Old instructions | New instructions | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #69478 | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#142](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/142): 2 inline | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#143](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/143): 2 inline | Same count; new API-proposal feedback mentions inherited-parameter name collisions, while old feedback does not. This is not a standalone finding of the exact case-insensitive collision. |
| #68633 | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#144](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/144): 5 inline | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#145](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/145): 6 inline | Both identify quiescence/disposal deadlock; only new identifies synchronous disconnect suppressing `JS.Error`. |
| #67314 | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#146](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/146): 4 inline | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#147](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/147): 5 inline | Both identify the vacuous test. New separates the managed rendered-class contract (.NET rendering test) from computed indicator styling (Selenium), rather than combining them into a browser-test request. |
| #69705, intended-silent documentation control | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#148](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/148): 1 inline | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#149](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/149): 1 inline | Neither stays silent; both request a renderer-attachment retry/reselection clarification. |
| #69706, intended-silent documentation control | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#150](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/150): 0 inline | [PureWeen/aspnetcore#151](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/151): 1 inline | Silence regression: new adds a recommendation to make compatibility-break approval explicit. |

These are mixed, exploratory, single-run output observations, including ties and a control regression. Comment counts are not correctness scores. Other comments were not independently adjudicated, and nondeterminism prevents attributing every difference to the instructions. No overall CCR improvement, accuracy, or recall claim is made.

Fixes: N/A (guidance-only change; no linked issue).

Skip public build and quarantined PR validation for skill-eval-only changes.

## Description

#70411 ran product builds and quarantined tests despite changing only guidance and skill-eval inputs. #70427 shows the narrower case with only two skill-eval files.

This adds `eng/skill-evals/*` to the PR exclusions in `ci-public.yml` and `quarantined-pr.yml`. It adds the same path to `report-green.yml` so Build Analysis still has a reporting job.

Merged #70635 provides the existing-filter control. Every changed file is under `.github/`, including nested Python and YAML files. Its checks show `aspnetcore-ci` and `aspnetcore-quarantined-pr` as `NEUTRAL`, and `aspnetcore-always-green` as `SUCCESS`. This demonstrates descendant matching for the existing `.github/*` filter. The new path uses the same filter shape.

`eng/skill-evals` has no project files. Product project selection and the root npm workspaces do not include it. `.github/workflows/skill-evals.yml` already validates its PR changes.

This PR changes three lines only. It preserves all existing filters, product-code eligibility, scheduled builds, and `ci.yml`.

**Open question:** Components E2E ran on changes that matched its existing exclusions. This PR leaves both Components E2E pipelines unchanged. It does not claim to skip every pipeline for #70411-shaped changes.

**Validation**

- `python -c "import pathlib,yaml; files=['ci-public.yml','quarantined-pr.yml','report-green.yml']; [yaml.safe_load((pathlib.Path('.azure')/'pipelines'/f).read_text()) for f in files]; print('PASS: all three edited YAML files parse')"`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- YAML structure comparison: passed. Only the three intended path entries change.
- Independent review completed before push. The final scope omits the uncertain pipeline changes identified during review.
- Product builds and tests: not run. This PR changes trigger filters only.
- Azure has not evaluated the new eval-only filter in a live PR event. The historical control supports the filter shape, not live verification of this change.

Related examples: #70411 and #70427. This PR does not close either PR or a separate issue.

Issues.Title: Add aspnet-build-triage and update-npm-dependencies agent skills
Issues.Body:
Adds two agent skills for the aspnet-build rotation:

- **`aspnet-build-triage`**: lists everything that needs the build-duty person's attention, grouped by category:
  - Maestro dependency and codeflow PRs, inter-branch merges, test-quarantine PRs, Dependabot PRs and localization PRs.
  - dotnet/dotnet PRs where a developer pinged `@dotnet/aspnet-build`.
  - Servicing PRs that are ready to merge, with the monthly release each would ship in (read from the DevDiv servicing schedule).
  - High and critical Component Governance security alerts on `main` and the supported release branches, with fix guidance.
  - Recent failures of the test-quarantine and Dependabot workflows that haven't been fixed.

  It can also retry failed CI on servicing PRs, check that the [dotnet/arcade-skills](https://github.com/dotnet/arcade-skills) and [dotnet/skills](https://github.com/dotnet/skills) plugins used for investigating failures are installed, and email the report once or on a schedule when the user asks. It never merges on the user's behalf, and it reminds the user to elevate to admin before acting on `release/*` PRs.
- **`update-npm-dependencies`**: refreshes npm lockfiles and ingests new packages into the `dotnet-public-npm` feed, respecting the 7-day quarantine. The triage skill points to it for npm Component Governance alerts.

The scripts are Python 3.9+, run on macOS, Linux and Windows, and have unit tests in `.github/skills/aspnet-build-triage/tests`.

Honor Kestrel port overrides when legacy startup services fail

## Description

With a legacy `IWebHostBuilder`, `CaptureStartupErrors(true)`, and an exception in `Startup.ConfigureServices`, the host skips startup filters but still starts Kestrel to serve the startup error page. Since the factory's port override is applied by a startup filter, `factory.UseKestrel(0)` is ignored on this path. Kestrel instead attempts to bind the application's configured URL, which can fail if that port is already in use.

Apply the requested port after building the legacy web host and before starting it. Keep the existing startup filter for generic and minimal hosts, reusing the address configuration logic without restoring the minimal-hosting startup race.

Add `RealServerPortOverrideTests.PortOverrideIsAppliedWhenStartupServicesThrow`. The test keeps the application's configured port occupied, throws from the real startup services path, and verifies that the factory serves the original startup error over HTTP on a different dynamic loopback port.

### Validation

```powershell
. .\activate.ps1
$env:ASPNETCORE_TEST_LOG_MAXPATH='32767'
dotnet test .\src\Mvc\test\Mvc.FunctionalTests\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.FunctionalTests.csproj --no-restore -p:NuGetAudit=false -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false -p:BuildNodeJS=false -p:StaticWebAssetsEnabled=false --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~RealServer' -v:q
```

Passed: **16**, failed: **0**, skipped: **0**.

Before the fix, the new regression fails with the expected occupied-port bind error; the six existing port-override tests pass. The same regression passes using the exact factory source from before #67714 and from after #67714 / before #70520, compiled against the remaining current source graph.

Validation covers real Kestrel sockets, legacy startup-error handling, generic/minimal hosting, and existing port-precedence scenarios. JavaScript/static assets and IIS native assets are disabled for this focused managed HTTP run; browser/IIS behavior and the full MVC suite were not validated.

Follow-up to #70520; historical context: #67714.

Cover QuickGrid keyboard activation and virtualized row focus restoration

## Description

Add five Selenium E2E cases for keyboard and focus behavior that the existing mouse-only `OnRowClickTriggersCallback` test does not cover:

- `OnRowClickKeyboardActivation`: Tab reaches successive clickable rows; Enter and Space each invoke the callback once with the correct item.
- `OnRowClickKeyboardActivationIgnoresInteractiveDescendants`: input and button key handling stays native and does not activate the containing row. Input key-up and button-click counters confirm the interactions occurred before checking the absence of a row callback.
- `VirtualizedRowRetainsFocusWhenItemsAreReplaced`: a real provider refresh removes the original non-first row and restores focus to its replacement after Enter and Space. Another refresh triggered outside the grid must not steal focus.

Reuse the existing QuickGrid test components with opt-in configurations. No shipping code or public API changes.

### Validation

Run on Windows with Chromium, using the repository SDK. Machine-specific `TEST_CHROME_BINARY` and result-output paths are omitted below.

```powershell
. .\activate.ps1
$env:ASPNETCORE_TEST_LOG_MAXPATH = '32767'
dotnet build src\Components\test\E2ETest\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj --no-restore -v:q -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false
dotnet test src\Components\test\E2ETest\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj --no-build --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.Tests.QuickGridTest'
```

- Targeted build: passed with zero warnings and errors. Full QuickGrid class: **19 passed, zero failed or skipped**. Two further fresh-process runs of the five new cases: **5/5 passed each**.
- Strict red/green: removing the keyboard listener fails both activation cases while the original mouse test passes; disabling focus restoration fails the replacement-focus assertion after confirming actual old-row removal; broadening the key handler to include descendants fails both nested-control cases. All five cases pass with the original shipping JS restored.
- Interactive validation in the canonical `BlazorWebAppPerPage` InteractiveServer sample: **10/10 scenarios passed**, including native controls, real row replacement, and outside-focus retention, with no page or console errors. No product defect found in the exercised scenarios.

The initial broad repository build was stopped after unrelated `Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.Embedded` namespace and WiX errors; the focused sample and E2E builds passed. Selenium exercised the WebAssembly host, with Server validated separately through the interactive sample. Other browser engines and the release backport were not validated.

Follow-up to #70248 and #70420.

Issues.Title: Identity: DataProtectorTokenProvider ignores TimeProvider, though the ASP.NET Core 11 release notes list token expiration
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

The ASP.NET Core 11 release notes ([TimeProvider support in ASP.NET Core Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11)) say:

> ASP.NET Core Identity now uses `TimeProvider` instead of `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` for all time-related operations.

> By using `TimeProvider`, you can more easily write deterministic tests for time-sensitive Identity features such as token expiration, lockout durations, and security stamp validation.

Lockout does follow the registered `TimeProvider` in 11.0.0 (`UserManager.UtcNow()` resolves it from the service provider, [UserManager.cs L2751-L2755](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v11.0.0/src/Identity/Extensions.Core/src/UserManager.cs#L2751-L2755)), and the security stamp validator takes it from `SecurityStampValidatorOptions.TimeProvider`.

Token expiration does not. `DataProtectorTokenProvider<TUser>` still stamps and checks tokens with the system clock:

- [L83](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v11.0.0/src/Identity/Core/src/DataProtectorTokenProvider.cs#L83): `writer.Write(DateTimeOffset.UtcNow);`
- [L118](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v11.0.0/src/Identity/Core/src/DataProtectorTokenProvider.cs#L118): `if (expirationTime < DateTimeOffset.UtcNow)`

`DataProtectionTokenProviderOptions` has no `TimeProvider`, and the class does not resolve one. `main` is the same today.

So the tokens made by `AddDefaultTokenProviders()` (email confirmation, password reset, change email) cannot be tested for expiration with a fake `TimeProvider`, contrary to the release notes.

### Expected Behavior

`DataProtectorTokenProvider` reads the time from the registered `TimeProvider` (falling back to `TimeProvider.System`), like `UserManager` does in 11.0, so a token's `TokenLifespan` can be tested with `FakeTimeProvider`. If that is not intended, the release notes should not list token expiration.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Register `FakeTimeProvider` (Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing 11.0.0) as the `TimeProvider` singleton, then `AddIdentity`/`AddIdentityCore` with `AddDefaultTokenProviders()`, and keep the default `TokenLifespan` of 1 day.
2. Create a password reset token with `UserManager.GeneratePasswordResetTokenAsync(user)`.
3. `fakeTimeProvider.Advance(TimeSpan.FromHours(25))`.
4. `UserManager.ResetPasswordAsync(user, token, newPassword)` still succeeds. The token was stamped and checked with the real clock, so it has not expired.

A lockout tested the same way, by advancing the fake clock past `DefaultLockoutTimeSpan`, behaves as expected.

### Exceptions (if any)

None.

### .NET Version

11.0.100 (runtime 11.0.0)

### Anything else?

On `release/10.0`, `UserManager` also used `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, so lockout is the part that changed in 11.0; the token provider did not.

Issues.Title: [review-pull-request] CCR overview cards deduplicate distinct anchored worker candidates without verification (#70532)
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

Part of EPIC #70231.

In `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/prepare-review.cs:513-528, 1554-1558` (`afdb030a14`), `ProjectFeedbackAsync` projects every entry from `pulls/{pr}/reviews` into `feedback.json`'s `reviews` array (`required/feedback/reviews/{id}.source`), including automated `copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]` `<!-- ccr-overview-v2 -->` overview cards. `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:228-229, 249-255, 365-366` instructs the coordinator to deduplicate candidates covered by an *"equivalent earlier issue, review, resolved inline comment, or current feedback"* into `EXISTING_FEEDBACK_COVERAGE`, without distinguishing topical coverage of an unanchored design question from an anchored changed-line candidate that has a different trigger and code mechanism.

#### Live occurrence: PR #70532 (run `43397825462`)

On [#70532](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70532) (*Fix ambiguous Blazor framework endpoints when mapping multiple roots*, [run `43397825462`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43397825462), frozen head `161ad276cf928913052abb4d23f0a6b5b3fa7014`), both routed specialist guide workers (`BlazorComponentsGuidance.md` and `CrossCuttingGuidance.md`) independently proposed an anchored P2 candidate at `src/Components/Endpoints/src/Builder/BlazorWebEndpointMatcherPolicy.cs:43`:

- **Worker candidate:** `BlazorWebEndpointMatcherPolicy.ApplyAsync` deduplicates duplicate framework endpoints across multiple `MapRazorComponents` roots by comparing `candidates[i].Endpoint.RequestDelegate == candidates[j].Endpoint.RequestDelegate` (delegate reference equality). When an application registers a delegate-wrapping convention via `RazorComponentsEndpointConventionBuilder.Add(b => { var next = b.RequestDelegate!; b.RequestDelegate = ctx => next(ctx); })`, `RazorComponentEndpointDataSource.AddFrameworkEndpoints` produces a distinct `RequestDelegate` per root, so `RequestDelegate == RequestDelegate` evaluates `false` and `DefaultEndpointSelector.cs:86-94` still throws `AmbiguousMatchException` on `/_framework/opaque-redirect` and the browser-tools settings path.
- **Coordinator bypass of verification via `EXISTING_FEEDBACK_COVERAGE`:** Instead of sending the anchored candidate to `review-candidate-verifier`, the coordinator skipped verification and returned `STATUS: NO_FINDINGS`, recording the candidate under `EXISTING_FEEDBACK_COVERAGE`:
  > *"Review 5887712198 already covers the source-supported equal-priority framework-endpoint concern involving differing root conventions and missing overlap coverage. Deduplication is neutral and does not endorse that review."*
- **Actual content of Review `5887712198` vs. independent verification:** [Review `5887712198`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70532#pullrequestreview-5887712198) (`copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`, state `COMMENTED`) is a top-level `<!-- ccr-overview-v2 -->` overview card containing `**No open issues** 🎉`, a changed-file summary table, and `### 🔵 Needs a closer look` (*"Human review is needed because the tie-breaker selects between equal-priority roots with different conventions or route values, and the supplied tests do not cover those overlaps"*), with zero inline comments and no mention of `BlazorWebEndpointMatcherPolicy.cs:43` or `RequestDelegate` wrapper identity. While that attention note legitimately covers a topical equal-priority root-convention question (as linked in [#70532 (comment)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70532#issuecomment-6853116119)), conflating it with the `RequestDelegate == RequestDelegate` wrapper candidate bypassed `review-candidate-verifier` (which in `#70532` comment `6853116119` independently evaluated that candidate as `DROP` / `contradicted` / `oldVsNew` because the ambiguity pre-existed `mergeBase`). - [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Don't let ReadFormAsync return null when the body completes on another thread

## Description

`InnerReadFormAsync` ends with `Form = formFields`, and the `Form` setter clears `_parsedFormTask`. When the body arrives on another thread, that continuation can run between `_parsedFormTask = InnerReadFormAsync(...)` and `return _parsedFormTask`, so `ReadFormAsync` returns null. Callers that await it directly, such as the OIDC `form_post` callback in the issue, then throw a `NullReferenceException`.

`ReadFormAsync` now reads `_parsedFormTask` once into a local, stores the new task in the field, and returns the local. Caching is unchanged: the field still holds the task until the read finishes, and is cleared when `Form` is set, as before.

I didn't add a unit test, because the window is between two adjacent statements and I couldn't find a way to hit it deterministically. I checked it with a stress program instead. It is based on the one in the issue: reader/writer thread pairs, with the writer completing the request body after a delay that adapts so it lands near the moment `ReadFormAsync` returns. Each run used 2 pairs for 20 seconds, alternating builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http` from `main` and from this branch (Release, Windows 11 x64, runtime 12.0.0-alpha.1.26565.104):

| Round | main: null tasks / reads | this branch: null tasks / reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 7 / 6,702,746 | 0 / 6,859,625 |
| 2 | 2 / 6,797,252 | 0 / 5,514,081 |
| 3 | 7 / 5,790,330 | 0 / 6,607,595 |
| 4 | 9 / 8,558,649 | 0 / 6,946,166 |
| 5 | 8 / 6,895,611 | 0 / 5,810,223 |

The existing `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Tests` pass.

Fixes #69744

# Fix race in ModelMetadata.GetHashCode

Compute the metadata identity hash during construction.

## Description

Replace the unsynchronized nullable hash cache with a hash computed in the `ModelMetadata` constructor. This prevents concurrent `GetHashCode()` calls from returning an indeterministic value under the race condition.

Fixes #59384

## Customer Impact

Concurrent initialization can cause record validation to throw “No property found that maps to constructor parameter” until the application restarts.

- [x] No

- [ ] High
- [x] Medium
- [ ] Low

The change computes the hash eagerly. The broader performance impact has not been measured.

## Verification

- [ ] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

- [x] N/A

Issues.Title: Fix static SSR ErrorBoundary failures when disposing named forms
Issues.Body: # Fix static SSR ErrorBoundary failures when disposing named forms - Fix static SSR requests returning HTTP 500 when an ErrorBoundary disposes a component containing a named form. - Render the boundary’s error content successfully instead of throwing a secondary exception. Before fix: After fix: ### Root Cause - A component’s named-form addition can be recorded before an exception triggers subtree disposal in the same batch. - Named-event removals are processed first, followed by additions referencing the disposed component. - Resolving that component’s form-mapping context throws a missing-component exception. ### Solution - Pass the current render batch’s disposed-component IDs into named-submit-event addition processing. - Skip additions belonging to those disposed components before resolving their form-mapping context. - Preserve registration and dispatch behavior for surviving forms without changing public APIs. ### Test Coverage - Verify boundary fallback rendering succeeds and the disposed form is no longer registered. - Verify fallback content can reuse the disposed form’s name and surviving forms outside the boundary remain dispatchable. - Sample validation confirms HTTP 500 becomes HTTP 200 with boundary fallback; no E2E tests added. Fixes #70640

Issues.Title: Apply the service check to [AsParameters] properties in the Request Delegate Generator
Issues.Body:
- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

## Description

The Request Delegate Generator emitted `IAcceptsMetadata` unconditionally for `[AsParameters]` types whose properties are classified as `JsonBodyOrService`, even when those properties were registered services. As a result a `GET` handler that takes its services through an `[AsParameters]` type advertised a JSON body and could be rejected by a catch-all endpoint, returning 404. Direct parameters already had the `IsService` check; only the `[AsParameters]` path missed it.

This makes `EmitJsonAcceptsMetadata` also classify the flattened properties of an `[AsParameters]` parameter, so the same `IsService` check is emitted and no `IAcceptsMetadata` is added when every `JsonBodyOrService` property is a registered service.

## Validation

- Added `AsParameters_WithOnlyServiceProperty_DoesNotAddAcceptsMetadata`, which fails on the generator path before this change and passes after.
- Regenerated `VerifyAsParametersBaseline` (the generated code now emits the `IsService` check).
- `dotnet test src/Http/Http.Extensions/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Extensions.Tests.csproj`: 2313 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #70638

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)

```
    "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",

      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    },

This used to work in ASP.NET Core 1.1 but no longer does. According to https://github.com/aspnet/DotNetTools/issues/404 the new format for ASP.NET Core 2.0 is:

```
   "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",

      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"

The problem with this is the hard coded `executablePath` which is Windows specific and the `workingDirectory` which is specific to wherever I did a Git clone on my local machine.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time" (#537)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages (latest patched version only) are currently [supported](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/aspnet#dotnet-core) on .NET Framework, following the support cycle for those .NET Framework versions. After April 13, 2027, this support will end regardless of the .NET Framework version in use.

Note that the [ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/aspnet/2.3-packages) include the Entity Framework 2.3 packages, which will end support on the same date.

## Impact of end of support

After ASP.NET Core 2.3 reaches end of support:

- No new security updates will be issued for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- Continuing to use an unsupported version may expose your applications to security vulnerabilities.
- Technical support will no longer be available for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- The ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages will be deprecated.

## Upgrade recommendation

We recommend upgrading to a [currently supported version of .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet), such as .NET 10 (LTS).

To help with the upgrade process, we recommend using [GitHub Copilot modernization](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/porting/github-copilot-app-modernization/overview), which provides AI-powered assistance to help you analyze, plan, and execute your migration to a modern .NET version.

Issues.Body:
Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

## Implementation

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

- Triggers on `issues.opened` and `issues.labeled` events with "Breaking change" label
- Creates issue in docs repo with:
  - Title: `[Breaking Change] <original title>`
  - Body: Link to source issue, full context
  - Labels: `breaking-change`, `aspnet/Announcements`
- Posts comment on source issue with link to docs issue

## Duplicate Prevention

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating
- Concurrency control keyed on issue number

## Error Handling

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:
- Comment listing failures → proceed with search
- Search failures → proceed with creation (fail open to avoid missing docs)
- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

## Setup Required

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Explicit minimal permissions: `issues: write`, `contents: read`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:
<details>
<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and MVC API analyzers are deprecated
Issues.Body:
## Description

The `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` MSBuild property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will now emit warning `ASPDEPR007`.

## Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

## Previous behavior

Previously, developers could set `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` in their Web SDK projects to enable MVC API analyzers without any warnings or deprecation notices.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The project would build successfully without any deprecation warnings.

## New behavior

Starting in .NET 10 Preview 7, when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will emit warning `ASPDEPR007`:

```
warning ASPDEPR007: The IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
```

The analyzers will continue to function, but developers will receive this deprecation warning during compilation.

## Type of breaking change

- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

## Reason for change

## Reason for change

The MVC API analyzers were originally introduced to help keep return types and attributes in sync for API controllers, ensuring consistency between method signatures and their corresponding OpenAPI documentation. These analyzers provided compile-time validation to catch mismatches between declared return types and the actual types returned by controller actions.

However, with the introduction of Minimal APIs and the `TypedResults` pattern, the .NET ecosystem has evolved toward a more type-safe approach for API development. `TypedResults` provides compile-time guarantees about response types without requiring additional analyzers, making the MVC API analyzers redundant for modern .NET applications. In .NET 10, `TypedResults` are supported in controller-based APIs.

**Previous approach with MVC API analyzers:**
```csharp
[HttpGet]
[ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)]
[ProducesResponseType(404)]
public async Task<ActionResult> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    if (product == null)
        return NotFound(); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType(404)
    
    return Ok(product); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)
}
```

**Or with controller actions using TypedResults:**
```csharp
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    return product == null 
        ? TypedResults.NotFound() 
        : TypedResults.Ok(product);
}
```

The `TypedResults` pattern eliminates the need for separate analyzers because the return type itself (`Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>`) explicitly declares all possible response types at compile time. This approach is more maintainable, provides better IntelliSense support, and automatically generates accurate OpenAPI documentation without additional tooling.

As the .NET ecosystem continues to embrace `TypedResults` as the recommended pattern for API development, the MVC API analyzers have become obsolete and are being deprecated to streamline the development experience.

## Recommended action

Developers should:

1. **Remove the deprecated property**: Remove `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` from your project files to eliminate the warning.

2. **Suppress the warning temporarily**: If you need to continue using the deprecated analyzers temporarily, you can suppress the warning:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);ASPDEPR007</NoWarn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

3. **Migrate to TypedResults**: Migrate to the `TypedResults` pattern documented above to ensure better consistency between application behavior and OpenAPI documentation.

- Associated MVC API analyzers included when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is `true`

### Description

The **Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client** NuGet package has been **deprecated** starting in **.NET 10 Preview 7**.  The package supplied MSBuild targets and CLI support (e.g., `dotnet openapi`, the `OpenApiReference` item group, and `OpenApiProjectReference` property) that generated OpenAPI-based client code during the build. Projects that reference the package will now receive a warning during build.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

Projects could add `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client" … />` and  `<OpenApiReference>` (or run `dotnet openapi`) to generate strongly-typed clients at build time.

 1. **Remove** any `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client" … />` from your project.  
        2. Replace `<OpenApiReference>` items or `dotnet openapi` commands with generator-specific tooling:  
           * **NSwag** – use `npx nswag` or `dotnet tool run nswag` with an `.nswag` config file.  
           * **Kiota** – install with `dotnet tool install -g Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota` and run `kiota generate`.  
           * **OpenAPI Generator** – invoke `openapi-generator-cli` via JAR or Docker.  
        3. Commit the generated client code or run generation in a custom pre-build step that does not rely on the removed package.

### Reason for change

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Forwarded Headers Middleware Now Ignores X-Forwarded-* Headers from Unknown Proxies
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17 and 9.0.6, the Forwarded Headers Middleware will ignore all `X-Forwarded-*` headers from proxies that are not explicitly configured as trusted.

### Version

.NET 8

### Previous behavior

Previously, the middleware, when not configured to use `X-Forwarded-For`, would process `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and `X-Forwarded-Host` headers from any source, potentially allowing malicious or misconfigured proxies/clients to spoof these headers and affect your application's understanding of client information.

### New behavior

With this change, only headers sent by known, trusted proxies (as configured via `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownProxies` and `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownNetworks`) will be processed. Headers from unknown sources will be ignored.

**This is a breaking change**: If your deployment relied on forwarded headers from proxies not configured in your application's trusted proxy list, those headers will no longer be honored.

This can cause behavior like infinite redirects if you're using the Https redirection middleware and using TLS termination in your proxy. Or authentication to fail if using TLS termination and expecting an https request.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The change was made for security hardening, as the proxy and IP lists weren't being applied in all cases.

### Recommended action

- **Review your deployment topology:**  
  Ensure that all legitimate proxy servers in front of your app are properly added to `KnownProxies` or `KnownNetworks` in your `ForwardedHeadersOptions` configuration.
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownProxies = { IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_PROXY_IP") }
  });
  ```
  Or, for a network:
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownNetworks = { new IPNetwork(IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_NETWORK_IP"), PREFIX_LENGTH) }
  });
  ```

- **If you wish to enable previous behavior:**  
  You may need to relax your configuration, but this is **not recommended** due to security risks. You can do this by clearing the `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` lists in `ForwardedHeadersOptions` to allow any proxy or network to forward these headers.

You can also set the `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` environment variable to true, which clears the lists and enables `ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto`.

For applications targeting .NET 9.0 or less, you can set the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.IgnoreUnknownProxiesWithoutFor` [AppContext](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/runtime-libraries/system-appcontext) switch to `"true"` or `1` to get back to the previous behavior. Alternatively, set the `MICROSOFT_ASPNETCORE_HTTPOVERRIDES_IGNORE_UNKNOWN_PROXIES_WITHOUT_FOR` environment variable.

> [!Note]
> In cloud environments, the proxy IP(s) can change over the lifetime of the app and `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` is sometimes used to make forwarded headers work.

### References

- [Forwarded Headers Middleware documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/proxy-load-balancer)

### Affected APIs

`UseForwardedHeaders();`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Legacy Mono and Emscripten JavaScript APIs are not exported to global namespace in Blazor WebAssembly applications
Issues.Body:
### Description

In previous versions of Blazor WebAssembly, legacy Mono and Emscripten APIs were exported to global namespace. 
From 9.0 those APIs are accessible throught Blazor.runtime object.

### Version

.NET 9 GA

### Previous behavior

Legacy Mono (MONO, BINDING) and Emscripten Module object was exported to global window object.
For example `window.Module.FS` returned emscripten virtual filesystem.

### New behavior

Emscripten Module object is now exported to `Blazor.runtime` object.
For example `Blazor.runtime.Module.FS` returns emscripten virtual filesystem.
Legacy Mono API for interop was removed completely (MONO and BINDING) and replaced with JSImport/JSExport.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The general goal is not to polute global namespace and keep all the APIs accessible from single Blazor object.

### Recommended action

Replace accessing Emscripten APIs from window object to Blazor.runtime object.

### Affected APIs

window.MONO.*
window.BINDING.*
window.Module.*
